title: GISS-2x2: Matched-State Geometry-Action Compatibility for Frozen Robot Policies
hook: Endpoint-equivalent geometry pairs can reveal whether a frozen VLA's current action chunk is specifically compatible with the geometry it saw. The reveal is a positive matched-state own-versus-cross native-success interaction, not a claim that the model recovered a globally necessary strategy graph.
hook_shape_rationale: This is a surprising empirical reveal because the named matched-state compatibility interaction can separate equal endpoint scores from geometry-specific current-action usefulness. Counter-intuitive minimalism was rejected because the candidate does not claim a reduction in parameters, data, or adaptation relative to the strongest baseline.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf tests whether endpoint task success under broad new-object, spatial, or long-horizon splits is sufficient evidence of functional-geometry generalization rather than an inherited evaluation assumption 鈥?stakes: published conclusions across benchmark, 3D-representation, scaffolded-stage, and replanning lineages may not transfer to cases where equal endpoints conceal different feasible strategy graphs.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by separately replayed common-prefix checkpoints whose complete non-geometry simulator, controller, RNG, action-frame, and fresh policy-history state is matched across A/B, followed by a four-cell first-chunk crossover with source-cache-free recipient continuation; corpus support is fulltext-degraded, so literature differentiation remains abstract-only.

core_mechanism: Instantiate RoboTwin 2.0 task pairs A and B with byte-identical instruction and terminal predicate, the same canonical target/reference asset frame and world pose, physical material, mass and inertia, robot/action specification, camera intrinsics/extrinsics, lighting, texture, background, controller configuration, and reset seed, while changing only the visible render and collision geometry relevant to manipulation. A self-built GISS manifest stores both mesh hashes and an attempted-pair record before policy inference. The matched-state producer uses the native reset when it is already a decision state; otherwise OMPL plans one pre-contact prefix against the union of A/B collision volumes, and that exact control prefix is replayed separately from fresh byte-identical resets in A and B rather than executed once in one scene and copied. This yields scene-specific checkpoints z_A and z_B whose immutable geometry handles differ but whose complete non-geometry transition state is equal: simulation clock, robot/object poses and velocities, joints, actuator/controller integrators and action queues, observation/history buffers, camera state, environment RNG/noise index, and a fresh policy inference-state template; target/reference contact caches must be empty. Equality is checked by field hashes plus an identical-geometry clone test that restores each checkpoint twice, applies the same no-contact action, and requires the next non-render state to match exactly; any mismatch makes the attempt ineligible. Visibility means the target/reference segmentation occupies at least v_min=0.01 of image pixels in both renders; v_min is fixed before outcomes for the main analysis, with coverage-only sensitivity at {0.005,0.01,0.02}. For each frozen OpenPI pi0.5 or released CLOVER policy, clone the same fresh inference/history template and reset the decode RNG/noise tape before each source query, then use ordinary RGB/proprioception/language inputs to obtain a_A from A and a_B from B; an identical-render repeat must decode byte-identically before that policy-run is eligible. Denormalize both chunks with the same policy-specific statistics into the same robot base-frame controller units, clipping, and native horizon, so cross execution never changes action convention. For every recipient r and source s, restore z_r, execute only a_s, discard all source-query model cache, and start a fresh recipient continuation from the actual post-chunk recipient observation under the same history-padding rule and decision-indexed noise tape until the native horizon, producing Y_rs. The matched-state compatibility interaction is I_MS=0.5[(E[Y_AA]-E[Y_AB])+(E[Y_BB]-E[Y_BA])]; a positive value is a scoped response contrast for matching-source current-chunk compatibility, not strategy identity, path necessity, full geometric understanding, or real-world transfer. The artifact reports both recipient contrasts, paired uncertainty when estimable, and coverage N_eligible/N_attempted over every preregistered request, with appearance-only four-cell pairs and matched state-jitter curves as falsifiers; no oracle label, geometry state, OMPL output, q, or phase string enters the tested policy.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
PREMISES LEDGER
P1: RoboTwin 2.0 exposes executable tasks, native terminal predicates, and simulator state control sufficient to build paired collision-geometry variants; this is plausible from its released simulator/data-generator role, but method details are fulltext-degraded and must be verified during implementation.
P2: The two shape renders are visible to the frozen policy while all non-geometry state fields at z are identical; otherwise source geometry is not the isolated intervention.
P3: Executing one native chunk and then restoring ordinary closed-loop control makes downstream native success sensitive to current-action compatibility rather than to an open-loop whole-trajectory splice; untested 鈥?falsification target.
P4 OBSERVATION-MODEL: pairs are purposively sampled from the predeclared GISS eligibility manifest, not an unbiased sample of all functional geometries, so inference is conditional on eligible RoboTwin task families and all exclusions must remain in the denominator.
ESTIMAND: I_MS is the mean, over preregistered eligible pair-state-policy-reset tuples, of the average within-recipient native-success effect of assigning the action chunk queried from matching rather than nonmatching source geometry at the identical checkpoint z; it is a bounded current-action compatibility response contrast, not an estimand of latent strategy understanding.
NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT
The naive diagnostic compares endpoint success across A and B or swaps same-index chunks from independently evolved policy trajectories. Branch (i): it silently assumes the compared chunks were queried at the same physical and controller state, which is false after geometry-dependent feedback evolution; GISS confronts that failure by producing z independently of the evaluated policy, restoring z before every query and execution, and crossing only one current chunk before closed-loop resumption. The 2x2 crossover is standard experimental-design machinery, but the unsolved domain-specific structure is that a robot action chunk changes contact state and all later feedback, so matching must occur before that chunk and recipient-scene fixed effects must be retained; OMPL is used only to certify a shared pre-contact prefix, never as the tested policy or a strategy oracle, avoiding regression to motion planning/TAMP as the claimed solution.
DESIGN RATIONALE
The endpoint-sufficiency gap needs one controlled instrument rather than separate strategy-label, localization, or adaptation modules, because the same four cells supply the comparison and its downstream native outcome. Exhaustive strategy grammars, switch-versus-nonswitch grouping, whole-trajectory crossover, and phase scaffolds were rejected because they reintroduce missing producers, post-treatment state mismatch, or contested definitions; an initial-decision/common-prefix checkpoint directly blocks those failure modes. COHERENCE BINDING. The causal interpretation is conditional on separately replayed A/B prefixes yielding equal complete non-geometry transition state, reset decoder RNG/history, one action frame, and fresh recipient-only continuation; appearance-only and identical-render controls diagnose render and stochastic shortcuts, while every jitter-invalid or otherwise excluded preregistered attempt remains visible in the coverage denominator.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Select executable RoboTwin 2.0 tasks with unchanged language and native terminal predicates; create A/B geometry variants in one canonical asset frame and write every preregistered attempted pair to a manifest with mesh hashes, world poses, physical properties, robot/action specification, reset seed, camera, lighting, texture, background, and controller configuration.
2. Use the native reset when eligible; otherwise plan one OMPL prefix against the union collision volume, then replay its exact controls separately from fresh byte-identical A and B resets without target/reference contact to produce z_A and z_B.
3. Hash-compare every complete non-geometry transition-state field, require empty target/reference contact caches, run the identical-geometry one-step clone test, verify collision-free validity and byte-identical instruction/goal, and apply visible_fraction >= v_min with v_min=0.01 fixed before outcomes; emit eligible/ineligible plus reason before policy inference.
4. For each frozen policy, clone one fresh policy inference/history template and reset the same decoder seed/noise tape before each A/B query; run an identical-render repeat determinism check, use ordinary RGB/proprioception/language only, and produce a_A,a_B.
5. Denormalize a_A,a_B through the same policy-specific normalizer into one robot base-frame action convention with identical clipping and nonempty native chunk horizon; reject the policy/task interface if these bindings differ.
6. For each (r,s), restore z_r, execute a_s open loop, discard source-query caches, and launch a fresh recipient continuation from the actual post-chunk observation using identical history padding and decision-indexed continuation noise; retain every collision and failure as an outcome.
7. Record Y_rs and compute both recipient contrasts and I_MS. Use pair/reset-blocked uncertainty only with multiple independent clusters; otherwise emit interval_not_estimable. Report N_eligible/N_attempted with every preregistered exclusion in the denominator, and emit not_estimable rather than zero when N_eligible=0.
8. Run the inherited protocol on appearance-only pairs with identical geometry/physics but changed texture/render nuisance, plus an identical-geometry identical-render decoder null, without relabeling outcomes.
9. Apply one shared seeded perturbation to continuous pose/velocity coordinates in a common tangent-space normalization for both scenes at every preregistered epsilon_z in {0,0.005,0.01,0.02}; keep discrete/controller/history fields fixed, designate 0.01 before outcomes as the headline value, rerun dual-scene eligibility, and retain jitter-invalid attempts in coverage.
10. Stratify endpoint-equal cases by I_MS and publish the coverage certificate and all controls; route to later adaptation only when a repeatable compatibility deficit and an external-controller upper bound coexist.
falsification_prediction: On preregistered eligible RoboTwin 2.0 pairs, run the frozen OpenPI pi0.5 and CLOVER four-cell checkpoint experiment and measure native task success plus I_MS; if visible geometry conditions useful current actions, I_MS should be positive even among endpoint-equal baseline strata. The one load-bearing variable is G_src, the source geometry rendered at the identical z to produce the current action chunk. As a non-tautological negative control, replace G_src's functional collision-geometry producer with appearance-only texture/render pairs that share one collision mesh and physics: the downstream native-success I_MS should return to its no-systematic-own-advantage baseline, while reversal or collapse under the smallest preregistered matched state jitter falsifies the claimed compatibility signal.
compute_budget: 12 A100 GPU-days for 64 paired states across four RoboTwin 2.0 task families, five paired reset seeds, two frozen policies, four crossover cells, controls, and reruns on the available 4xA100 system; approximately one engineer-week for the modest GISS manifest and state-restore tooling. $0 paid API cost because all policy, simulator, planner, and scoring components are local/open.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Abstract-only inference under fulltext_degraded evidence: RoboTwin 2.0 supplies scalable tasks and broad randomization, whereas GISS constructs byte-matched decision checkpoints and crosses one frozen-policy action chunk across paired functional collision geometries before recipient-scene closed-loop continuation.

Abstract-only inference: GemBench evaluates placements, objects, primitives, and long horizons, while GISS estimates a within-recipient matched-state geometry-action compatibility interaction at fixed instruction and terminal predicate.

Abstract-only inference: CoA-VLA supplies a fixed object/grasp/spatial/movement affordance chain to the policy, while GISS gives ordinary policies no phase scaffold and intervenes only on the visible geometry that produces the current chunk.

Abstract-only inference: CLOVER uses prediction error for closed-loop refinement and replanning, while GISS restores an identical pre-action state and estimates one-chunk source-geometry compatibility through a four-cell recipient-scene response contrast.

what_step_was_missed: The abstract does not construct a simulator checkpoint that is identical across paired functional geometries, query both frozen-policy chunks there, and execute each chunk in both recipient geometries before closed-loop resumption to estimate a within-recipient compatibility interaction; this is an abstract-only inference because full text was unavailable.
composition_note: A single controlled-diagnostic move is sufficient because the exact checkpoint producer, four-cell current-chunk intervention, independent simulator outcome, eligibility accounting, appearance control, and state-jitter falsifier form one deep instrument. Adding an audit, decomposition, or adaptation pattern would duplicate the interpretation, revive invalid chunk-index localization, or bolt a second paper onto this bounded diagnostic.
